# Golden fixtures

Frozen reference artefacts from real analyst runs. Committed in Phase A so that
every later phase — the Phase B visual oracle above all — has a fixed target to
validate against instead of a deck that has to be regenerated by hand.

These are **reference artefacts, not expected outputs.** Nothing asserts that a
fresh run reproduces them byte-for-byte: both deliverables embed a run date, and
the two rasterizers do not agree on pixels. They are here to be *measured*.

## Provenance

| Fixture | Source run | Run date | Plugin version |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pitch-*` | `Project Propel Holdings (TSXPRL)` — Propel Holdings Inc. (TSX:PRL) | 2026-07-16 | v0.5.34 (same-day) |
| `earnings-update-*` | `Project OTEX4` — Open Text Corporation | 2026-05-29 | v0.5.5-era |

The pitch pair is the most recent pitch run and matches the current code. The
earnings-update pair is the most recent earnings-update run there is — no EU run
has happened since v0.5.5, so it predates 29 releases. Its **structure is still
current** (5 slides: cover → overview → earnings summary → disclaimer → contact,
which is what today's `_KEEP_LIBRARY_INDICES` produces), but treat any *content*
detail as v0.5.5 behaviour, not as a specification. If an EU run happens before
Phase B lands, replace this pair and update this file.

Both subject companies are public issuers and every figure traces to a public
filing — but these are still INFOR client work product. Do not copy them
anywhere outside this repository.

## Known state — read before writing a checker against these

A checker run against these fixtures will produce findings. Some are correct
behaviour, one is a real defect. Do not "fix" the fixtures to silence either.

**Intentional, expected to stay:**

- `pitch-deck.pptx` slide 11 `Rectangle 3` — `[Placeholder for Comps Chart]`
- `pitch-deck.pptx` slide 12 `Rectangle 3` — `[Placeholder for Precedents Chart]`
  The comps and precedents slides ship as placeholders on purpose: their
  workbook tabs carry un-evaluated CapIQ array formulas, and the analyst
  refreshes in Excel, so there is nothing to render at build time.
- `earnings-update-deck.pptx` slide 2 `Rectangle 4` — `[Pie Chart Placeholder]`
  The LTM-revenue pie is filled by the pitch-only `financial-charts` stage; the
  earnings-update plan has no such stage, so the placeholder is correct.

**A real defect, found while freezing these (Phase A finding, deliberately not
fixed here — it belongs to the Phase B converge loop):**

- Three footnote shapes carry an unsubstituted `[x]` currency token:
  `pitch-deck.pptx` slide 9 (`Text Placeholder 4`, bare `[x]`) and slides 11 and
  12 (`Text Placeholder 1`, `Note: All figures in [x]$MM, except where indicated
  otherwise`). v0.5.34 added `pptx_helpers.fill_footnote_currency` and both
  assemblers call it, but not on every slide that carries the token — so a
  client-facing deck shipped with a literal `[x]` on it. This is exactly the
  bug class the migration plan is built around: valid XML, invisible to
  python-pptx assertions, visible to anyone who opens the file.

  It is a good first target for `deck_contract.py`'s forbidden-string scan, and
  a checker that does **not** flag it is under-specified.

**Clean:** neither deck contains `#N/A`, `#REF!`, or `{{` — the v0.5.16 /
v0.5.33 cross-tab relink and deletion gate did their job on the pitch run.

## Render parity

`test_render_parity.py` renders `pitch-deck.pptx` through both backends
(LibreOffice, and PowerPoint COM where available) and asserts they agree on
slide count, raster dimensions, and per-slide ink geometry. That test is the
executable form of the Phase A exit criterion.
